ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In 1831, Faraday demonstrated at a meeting the disk generator he invented (Figure A). It was made using the principle of electromagnetic induction and was the first generator in human history. Figure B is a schematic diagram of this disk generator: the copper disk is mounted on a horizontal copper shaft, and its edge is exactly between the two magnetic poles; two copper pieces C and D are respectively in good contact with the rotating shaft and the edge of the copper disk. When the copper disk is made to rotate, current passes through the resistor R. If the applied magnetic field is a uniform magnetic field, the total resistance of the circuit is constant, and viewed from left to right, the copper disk rotates uniformly in the clockwise direction, and the CRD plane is perpendicular to the plane of the copper disk, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Keep the copper disk stationary, and the magnetic field changes into an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk; then current is generated in the copper disk

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When keeping the copper disk motionless, if the magnetic field becomes an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk, will a current be produced in the copper disk?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Keep the copper disk stationary, and the magnetic field changes into an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk; then current is generated in the copper disk
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a physical photo of a Faraday disk generator; in the schematic diagram on the right side there is a vertically placed circular copper disk, a contact point C is marked near the center of the disk, a contact point D is marked near the edge of the disk, the external resistor R and C, D constitute an external circuit, and the magnetic-field arrows pass through the copper disk along the horizontal direction, with the direction perpendicular to the plane of the copper disk. Then reason: the question is changed to keeping the copper disk motionless, while the magnetic field becomes an alternating magnetic field whose direction is perpendicular to the copper disk. Any circular path in the copper disk centered on the center of the disk can be regarded as a closed loop inside the conductor. Since the magnetic field is perpendicular to the copper disk and changes with time, the magnetic flux Φ=B(t)S enclosed by this circular loop also changes with time, so dΦ/dt is not zero. According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, an induced electromotive force will be produced in the closed path. The copper disk itself is a conductor, so an induced current will form in the disk, namely an eddy current.
